newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T says no truth in fighting fund story.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T says no truth in fighting fund story.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc said on Monday there was no truth in a Sunday Telegraph newspaper story that the company had approached other cigarette makers to set up an industry-wide fighting fund.
"There is no basis for this story. They have been misled by someone," said Ralph Edmondson, B.A.T's investment relations manager.

The newspaper reported that B.A.T had contacted rival cigarette makers Philip Morris Cos Inc, R.J. Reynolds and Lorillard to form an industry-wide $3 billion fighting fund and insurance pool to cope with tobacco-related litigation.
B.A.T shares were up 17p in morning trade at 510p amid renewed hope, fired by weekend press reports, of a settlement in U.S. tobacco lawsuits.
The company's strategy on the demerger of its tobacco and financial services operations had also not changed, said investor relations assistant Denise Hart.
"The chairman said at the full year there are no sacred cows, we are looking at the businesses and what we can do to enhance shareholder value," she said.

The Times newspaper reported today that B.A.T was under pressure to bring forward a demerger of its tobacco and financial services operations and that it had decided a demerger could take place by the end of the year. -- Tim Farrand, +44 171 542 6437
